eta_points.name: West Tekong Buoy (line to point NE of Pulau Ubin)
point northeast of Pulau Ubin (or Long 103°59.53'E northwards off E end of Pulau Ubin)

update_points.name: West Tekong Buoy (eastbound via Nenas Channel)

rules: Max speed 12 kn in the East Johor Strait; 6 kn passing the yards and Changi Sailing Club area (approx 01°23.6'N 103°58.7'E).
No night towing (1900-0630) between the Causeway and Angler Buoy.
No vessel south of the line CAAS Buoy 1 (01°23.55'N 103°59.94'E; longitude printed with 'N' in the source, a misprint) to CAAS Buoy 2 (01°23.68'N 103°59.60'E).
No stopping or anchoring in the TIA; report to Sembawang Control at once if forced to in an emergency.
Report ETA changes at once: 2 min for Angler, Points 1 and 2, Paku, Malang Papan, West Tekong, NE Pulau Ubin; 15 min for Seletar Buoy.

reports.who: Owner, agent or master of passenger ships (incl. HSC), cargo ships of 500 GT and above, mobile offshore units
reports.when: At least 24 h before arrival; if from a nearby port under 24 h steaming, immediately on departure from that port
reports.what: Pre-Arrival Notification (PAN form v11.0): ship particulars and drafts, air draft, CSO and agent contacts, arrival voyage (facility, ETA/ETD, purpose), DG/HNS on board Y/N, ship security level, last 10 port calls with security levels, last 5 STS activities, armed guards, stowaways/rescued persons, arms on board, BCC/CLC/ISSC, Green Ship Programme fuel, BWM certificate and BWMS status, sulphur compliance method and scrubber type, FONOR, drones, declarant and ship position
reports.how: Email isps@mpa.gov.sg (Port Security Unit, tel +65 6221 3127); Singapore-based agent may submit via digitalPORT@SG. Once PAN is submitted, no separate NOA is needed. (MPA PAN web page still mentions fax +65 6221 3036 and 'Marinet'; the 2024 circular names email and digitalPORT@SG.)

reports.who: Owner, agent, master or person in charge of vessels under 500 GT
reports.when: At least 12 h before arrival
reports.what: Notice of Arrival (NOA) in the PC 14/2024 Annex B Appendix 2 format (incl. last port, height, arms on board, drones, remarks on defects/fire hazards/damage/assistance needed)
reports.how: Upload via digitalPORT@SG, or email noa@mpa.gov.sg, or fax +65 6224 5776

reports.who: Note on older NOA rule
reports.when: MPA 'Vessels Arriving' page still describes NOA for passenger vessels or 300 GT+: 12 h before arrival, on departure if from a port under 12 h away, 24 h if carrying bulk HNS (PC 15/1998)
reports.what: Slop/sludge to be declared in NOA item 11 if residues will be discharged in port
reports.how: noa@mpa.gov.sg, fax +65 6224 5776, telex RS 34970
reports.status: Page text appears older than PC 14/2024 (which makes PAN replace NOA for 500 GT+). Treat PC 14/2024 as current; the page is shown for completeness.

reports.who: Single hulled tankers of 5000 DWT and above
reports.when: At least 24 h before arrival, or immediately on departure from a nearby port under 24 h steaming
reports.what: Pre-arrival declaration form for single hulled tankers to the Port Master
reports.how: Fax (65) 6224 5776 or telex RS 34970

reports.who: Owner, agent or master of vessels carrying or intending to load bulk HNS (MARPOL Annex II NLS, IBC, IGC, IMSBC cargoes, and their residues)
reports.when: 24 h before arrival, or 24 h before loading if already in port
reports.what: Bulk HNS notification
reports.how: digitalPORT@SG (hazmat@mpa.gov.sg, +65 6325 2421)

reports.who: Owner, agent or master of vessels arriving with packaged dangerous goods, or onto which DG will be loaded

reports.what: DG declaration
reports.how: PSA terminals: PSA PORTNET; Jurong Port: JP-Online; other locations e.g. anchorages: digitalPORT@SG

reports.who: Vessels of 300 GT or more, tugs towing/pushing with combined 300 GT or more, any passenger vessel, intending to call at Singapore
reports.when: Confirmation of arrival: when at the designated reporting point on entering the VTIS area
reports.what: Vessel name; call sign; present location (with reference to a reporting point, e.g. when Horsburgh Lt is abeam); number of passengers and crew (passenger vessels only); ETA at first destination in port or name of the pilot boarding ground if taking a pilot; height if different from the NOA/PAN
reports.how: VHF to VTIS: East VHF 10 when abeam Horsburgh Lt (01°19.814'N 104°24.337'E), Karang Galang Lt (01°09.577'N 104°11.365'E) or Eastern Buoy (01°17.865'N 104°05.894'E); Central VHF 14 when joining the TSS lane between 103°44.6'E and 104°02.1'E after leaving port or anchorages; West VHF 73 when abeam Pulau Jangkat Beacon (00°57.895'N 103°42.619'E) or Pulau Iyu Kechil (01°11.479'N 103°21.140'E). From other directions call the appropriate VTIS on entering the area and give bearing and distance from a reference point.

reports.who: Vessels of 300 GT and above; tugs towing/pushing with combined 300 GT and above; all passenger vessels; vessels 30 m or more in length; vessels 30 m or more in height
reports.when: Channel Information Report: arriving vessel before entering the port; any vessel before moving within or leaving the port. Permission needed before entering, moving within or leaving a reporting sector.
reports.what: Name or call sign; draft; present location (position when entering port limit); destination (new location in port or bound for sea); height; remarks (Appendix 5 summary also lists next port)
reports.how: VHF to the control station of the sector (East Control 12, Keppel Control 05, Cruise Bay Control 05, Pasir Panjang Control 18, Sinki Control 68, Jurong Control 22, West Control 68, Sembawang Control 21). English, local time, 24-hour clock.

reports.who: Same vessels as above
reports.when: Arrival Report: on arrival at the destination in port (berth or anchorage)
reports.what: Terminal: name or call sign, arrival date and time, berth and terminal. Anchorage: name or call sign, arrival date and time, anchorage name, bearing and distance from a reference point (Eastern Buoy 01°17.9'N 104°05.9'E; Amber Beacon 01°17.9'N 103°54.3'E; Rimau Beacon 01°15.5'N 103°48.4'E; Sultan Shoal Lt Ho 01°14.4'N 103°38.9'E). Continuous VHF watch at anchor.
reports.how: VHF to the sector control station
reports.note: SPI 2025 pilotage section para 21: all vessels above 300 GT report final anchored position by bearing and distance from these reference points.

reports.who: Same vessels as above
reports.when: Underway Report: when underway in a channel after leaving an anchorage or berth, and when passing abeam each reporting point in PC 06/2021 Appendix 4
reports.what: Name or call sign; present location (e.g. abeam NE Corridor Buoy). Keep continuous watch on the sector channel; additional watch on VHF 16 advised.
reports.how: VHF to the sector control station

reports.who: All vessels regardless of GT entering or leaving the West Johor Strait reporting sector (including those transiting without calling at Singapore)
reports.when: Before entering and before leaving the sector
reports.what: Name or call sign; draft; present location; destination; height; remarks
reports.how: Jurong Control VHF 22; if no VHF, telephone POCC +65 6325 2493/4

reports.who: Vessels of 2000 GT or more, vessels over 30 m height, tugs/tows of 2000 GT or more or over 30 m height, in the East Johor Strait
reports.when: Before entering, manoeuvring within or leaving the East Johor Strait (clearance required); again when passing each ETA reporting point; ETA updates at Kees Beacon / Punggol and Squance Buoys / West Tekong Buoy / when leaving Sungai Johor
reports.what: Name; call sign; present location; destination; draft; height; remarks; ETAs at the line West Tekong Buoy - NE Pulau Ubin, Angler Buoy, Point 1, Point 2, Paku Buoy abeam, Malang Papan Beacon abeam, Seletar Buoy abeam (ETAs are used to coordinate aircraft traffic)
reports.how: Sembawang Control VHF 21 (reserved VHF 13); continuous watch on VHF 21 underway or at anchor in EJS; tel 6481 5848, scc@mpa.gov.sg

reports.who: Owner, agent or master
reports.when: Within 24 h of arrival
reports.what: Arrival General Declaration (vessel details, purpose of call, arrival date/time, last port, location on arrival, grid reference, master, crew, passengers, cargo). First call: Application of Vessel Record Creation first; renamed vessel: Application for Change of Vessel Particulars first.
reports.how: digitalPORT@SG to MPA Marine Licensing and Permits (MLP)

reports.who: Owner, agent or master
reports.when: Before departure (combined Arrival and Departure GD allowed for stays of 3 days or less)
reports.what: Departure General Declaration (vessel details, purpose, departure date/time, next port, master, crew, passengers, cargo); a Port Clearance Certificate is generated on submission. Vessel must leave within 48 h of port clearance (or shorter period set by the Port Master); agent returns the PCC within 6 h after expiry if not used.
reports.how: digitalPORT@SG to MLP

reports.who: Vessels using pilots
reports.when: Order pilotage directly with PSA Marine Pte Ltd (the pilotage service provider)
reports.what: Pilot booking. Lead times (6 h before service required time; BGPAN pre-arrival notice to the pilot office 72 h to 2.5 h before boarding ground arrival; confirmation 2 h before) were seen only on an unofficial mirror of the PSA Marine page: UNCONFIRMED.
reports.how: PSA Marine; Singapore Pilots VHF 20 (157.000 / 161.600 MHz) for pilotage service and information. Vessels at anchor needing a pilot at night show white-white-red all-round lights vertically; by day flag G.

The SPI table positions are least-depth high spots, not anchorage limits, so they are not recorded. Purposes: MPA says each anchorage purpose is defined in the eGazette; only what the name implies is known.
